shortDescription: The South African rand firmed on Wednesday as the dollar weakened after U.S. private payrolls data showing slower job growth, which reinforced expectations of a more cautious Federal Reserve policy path.

children: The South African rand firmed on Wednesday as the dollar weakened after U.S. private payrolls data showing slower job growth, which reinforced expectations of a more cautious Federal Reserve policy path.
At 1413 GMT the rand traded at 16.0425 against the dollar
, up around 0.8% from its previous close, recovering some losses after recent gains were eroded by renewed tensions in the

was last down about 0.1% against a basket of currencies. U.S. private payrolls increased less than expected in August as gains in the education and health services sector were offset by job losses in manufacturing and a few other industries.
This provided some support for risk-sensitive currencies such as the rand, which often takes its cues from global market sentiment and U.S. economic and monetary policy developments.
Investor attention will remain on the U.S., with additional labour market data due before the end of the week.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) strengthened, as the yield fell 2.5 basis points to 8.655%.
